rites.name: Amiallastus
rites.text: Amiallastus is the concept of a tone held in the Singing, the sounding by which the first roots of Miinnora condensed into matter. Within the Holy Age its name is spoken in the flame-lit temples of the orders, where it is taken as the pattern from which every resonant thing is shaped.

rites.name: Lyaraemae
rites.text: Lyaraemae is the concept of the first sounding that condensed the roots of Miinnora, a note held long enough to become ground and sky. In the Age of Sundering it is remembered as the force that let the broken landfalls find their old bonds again.

rites.name: Orallor
rites.text: Orallor is the concept of the mutual sending that let the Courts of Miinnora bind their doors between worlds during the Age of Sundering. Within the great councils it stands as the principle that a gate holds only while both sides consent to it.

rites.name: Drarneld
rites.text: Drarneld is the concept of binding sworn oaths into the walls of the Courts, the thread that holds a promise to its keeper across the shifting doors between worlds. In the Age of Sundering it was the discipline that let councils seal their agreements when landfall broke the older compacts.

rites.name: Elaeniel
rites.text: Elaeniel is the quiet moment when the makers press the first threads of the Weave into the soil of Miinnora, and the sleeping powers beneath the groves stir without waking. The planting sends a slow tide of stillness outward, settling the wild magic into patterns that the early kingdoms would later call their roots.

rites.name: Sisheth
rites.text: Sisheth is a concept of Miinnora's Seeding, the time when makers plant the Weave and dormant powers lie quiet beneath the world. It belongs to the Holy Age, a period of flame, temples and sworn orders that gathered their strength around these sleeping forces. Its meaning is the promise of waking, not the waking itself.

rites.name: Thizyushis
rites.text: Thizyushis is the concept of the Walled Age in Miinnora, the long centuries when holding walls, sworn orders, and the first crossings of the gaps between districts defined what it meant to keep a thing whole. Its presence is felt in every mortared stone and every oath kept through a siege.
